sections.overview: Monticolomys koopmani is a Malagasy rodent in the endemic family Nesomyidae, known from the central and southern highlands.
sections.identification: The taxonomic accounts consulted establish its identity as a nesomyid rodent but do not provide a concise field description or diagnostic measurements.
sections.habitat: Mammal Species of the World records it in scattered sclerophyllous montane forest at about 1.6–2 km in eastern Madagascar; its type locality is at about 1.8 km.
sections.diet: The taxonomic and distribution sources reviewed do not document a species-specific diet, so particular foods are left unspecified.
sections.behavior: The sources reviewed do not establish its daily activity pattern or locomotion, so these behaviours remain undescribed here.
sections.reproduction: The sources reviewed provide no verified breeding dates, litter size or gestation data for this species.
sections.ecology: Molecular phylogenies consistently place Monticolomys as the sister genus of Macrotarsomys, another Malagasy nesomyine lineage.
sections.conservation: The American Society of Mammalogists’ Mammal Diversity Database reports the IUCN category Least Concern, citing the 2024 Red List record.
